issue_context.title: Extract tplink switch energy attributes into sensors
issue_context.body:
This issue is for the switch platform of the tplink integration.

The switch integration has embedded sensors for energy usage. This is no longer the preferred approach. Integrations using this approach should turn this data into standalone sensors.

This is important because Home Assistant is going to introduce home energy management (HEM) in 2021.8. HEM will be able to consume the data if it is exposed as standalone sensors.

To make sure that the sensors that represent total kWh is usable for HEM, set `state_class` to `measurement` and set `last_reset` to the timestamp of when the meter got reset (midnight if daily etc). [See sensor documentation for more information.](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor)

[Link to the architecture discussion.](https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/discussions/579)
comments: is there already someone working on? if not, I would do...
I don't think there is. Would love if you pick it up. I'm prioritizing reviewing PRs that touch this and similar issues.

... after some hours of investigating it figured that it would be more pain as thought :see_no_evil:
the `tplink` integration needs first a re-writing to implement `DataUpdateCoordinator` for each device, so that multiple sensors per device can be implemented, without massively increase the count of api calls against the devices ... this honestly is a bit to much needed effort, which I can not spend for now :confused:
plans change, so I found time to implement the `DataUpdateCoordinator` and also add new sensor platform to tplink

review_comments: Please don't use switch integration attribute constants to describe sensors. Define attributes in the sensor platform instead.
Please use `hass.async_add_executor_job` to schedule jobs on the executor. `hass.async_add_job` is legacy for normal use.
Check the precense or absence of this entity state in the core state machine instead.

Please don't assert integration details like hass.data in the tests. Assert core state.

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/development_testing#writing-tests-for-integrations
I'd move this constant to the sensor platform to avoid importing from the sensor integration here. That latter is the responsibility of the sensor platform.
Don't patch our code, patch the library.
